title: Per-agent OPFS work dirs with git merge at burst end
description: VISION v1's merge discipline: each spawned agent gets an isolated workspace (per-agent OPFS dir or VFS namespace), works on a branch, and the dashboard merges results at burst end (isomorphic-git or the github-backend Git Data API path). Today agents share nothing and fleet_report carries prose only — parallel file edits from two agents cannot be reconciled.
acceptance_criteria: Burst of 2 agents editing the same checkout produces two branches and a dashboard-side merge (or conflict report); nothing merges silently.
close_reason: Per-tab sessionStorage checkout isolation (token stays shared); branch-per-agent convention in spawn briefing; github_merge integrates heads via GitHub merges API with explicit conflict reporting (never force-merges), auto-creating the base; github_branches for discovery. Verified: isolation across two tabs, and clean/uptodate/conflict merge paths.

title: Fleet shares one brain: quipu in a SharedWorker
description: Agent tabs currently fall back to in-memory quipu because the opfs-sahpool VFS is single-owner (first tab wins). Host the quipu-wasm store in a SharedWorker instead of a per-tab dedicated Worker so every same-origin tab talks to ONE store over ports — dashboard writes an episode, spawned agents query it instantly. Fallback to the dedicated worker where SharedWorker is unavailable (Chrome for Android). This is the enabler for VISION v2 'grounded cheap agents' inside a burst.
acceptance_criteria: Two tabs: episode written in tab A is quipu_query-visible in tab B without reload; OPFS persistence retained; single-tab behavior unchanged on browsers without SharedWorker.
close_reason: Leader-elected shared store: Web Locks pick a host tab whose dedicated worker owns OPFS; other tabs RPC over BroadcastChannel; takeover on leader death re-opens the same bytes. Verified: A→B and B→A visibility without reload, and data survival across leader death.

title: In-browser bash execution: bash-backend.js in-page MCP server
description: Add bash execution support to creel: a new in-page MCP server (inpage:bash) exposing bash_exec — a pure-JS POSIX-ish bash interpreter over the shared VFS (pipes, redirection, quoting, vars, command substitution, arithmetic, globs, core utilities). No server, no container: fits creel's 'the sandbox is the browser' bet. Wire into onepagent.html, sw.js cache, justfile check; node:test suite.

title: Compile yupana to wasm for in-page structural analysis in creel
description: Bring yupana (live per-tenant code structure — call graph, refs, dataflow, impact) into creel as a fourth in-page knowledge source alongside quipu, so agents get 'what calls this / what will this break' on the VFS/checkout with zero network. Follows quipu's wasm playbook exactly (docs/design/wasm-support.md in quipu): (1) feature-gate the native stack off default — tokio 'full', clap, axum/rmcp (mcp feature), daemon/watch/git shell-outs — behind cfg(not(target_arch=wasm32)); (2) tree-sitter is the hard blocker: it compiles C grammars via cc, no libc on wasm32 — swap to web-tree-sitter (wasm grammars loaded at runtime) or tree-sitter's own wasm build, OR ship a wasm-bindgen dispatch that calls web-tree-sitter from JS and keeps only the graph/query layer in Rust; (3) getrandom wasm_js backend + RUSTFLAGS; (4) a creel-quipu-provider-style crate (wasm/yupana-provider) exposing analyze(files) + the yupana_* tool surface via wasm-bindgen, hosted in a worker like quipu; (5) feed it the FILES panel / github-checkout tree. Coordinate with whoever owns yupana's roadmap — the native-side feature-gating belongs in yupana proper (mirrors quipu-gsg/quipu-as2), the provider crate lives in creel.
acceptance_criteria: yupana lib compiles for wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features; a creel worker exposes yupana_analyze + refs/impact over the inpage MCP transport against VFS files; graph explorer or a tool shows call-graph facts; degrades gracefully when the bundle is absent (like quipu-wasm).

title: Code execution on the Pages origin: COI headers or Vivari
description: NodeExec (WebContainer) needs SharedArrayBuffer, which needs cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP) — GitHub Pages sets neither, so on the deployed origin only Pyodide runs. Options per VISION constraints: (a) coi-serviceworker shim (works on Pages, but breaks cross-origin fetches lacking CORP — audit DeepSeek/OpenRouter calls first), (b) swap WebContainer for Vivari (MIT, no COI requirement claim to verify, removes the commercial-license question), (c) accept Python-first and document it. Decide and implement.
acceptance_criteria: Either NodeExec boots on the deployed Pages site with LLM calls still working, or the README states Python-first with the reasoning.

title: The measurement: grounded vs ungrounded cheap agents
description: The bet VISION v2 stands on, still unmeasured: task success rate and cost-per-completed-task of small-model agents (deepseek-v4-flash) with vs without quipu grounding, vs one frontier agent. Design a small task suite that needs prior knowledge (seed the graph first), run bursts each way, capture tokens+outcomes via fleet_report, and write the numbers into docs/. The fleet + comms + shared-brain machinery makes this runnable now.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible bench doc with success-rate and cost columns for grounded/ungrounded/frontier; conclusions folded back into VISION.

title: Knowledge pack loader: fetch a distilled .db at session start
description: VISION v2: 'the graph snapshot ships to the browser read-only (fetched at session start)'. quipu-wasm can already open_from_bytes and CreelQuipu.importDb exists, but there is no fetch-a-pack flow: a configurable pack URL (or file picker) loaded at boot, shown in quipu_wasm_status, with the open question from VISION (whole pack vs topic-windowed via one server-side search) recorded as a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Setting a pack URL loads it at boot into the store (or a named graph); status reports pack provenance; works on the Pages deploy.

title: Work-queue leasing: N tasks, M agents, drain and requeue
description: VISION v1 burst controls. Today fleet_spawn is 1 task = 1 tab at spawn time. Add a task queue agents lease from via Web Locks (the lock auto-release on tab death requeues the task), fleet_drain (agents finish current task then stop claiming), and spawn-N-workers-against-queue. The leasing primitive is the piece that makes tab death recoverable instead of just visible.
acceptance_criteria: Queue of 5 tasks, 2 agent tabs: all 5 complete; killing a tab mid-task requeues it; fleet_drain stops claiming without killing work in flight.
close_reason: fleet_enqueue/spawn_workers/drain with Web Lock leasing; death-requeue and non-reentrant claiming verified across real tabs (4 tasks / 2 workers, kill mid-task recovered).

title: Align the creel world model with camayoc ontology discipline
description: creel-world-model-v1 mints ad-hoc types (Role, Subsystem, Surface, ToolServer) straight into the shared store. Camayoc owns what facts MEAN for the stack: competency questions before classes, reuse before minting (aegis:/prov:/quipu: first), rdfs:range not rdfs:domain. Write the competency questions the world model answers ('who dispatches?', 'what tools serve the root pane?', 'what conventions bind a bobbin?'), align/rename terms to stack vocabularies, and bump to creel-world-model-v2 with a migration note. The versioned marker node makes the re-seed safe.
acceptance_criteria: Competency questions documented; v2 model uses reused vocabulary where it exists; agents' quipu_cord entrypoint unchanged.

title: Ask for durable storage: navigator.storage.persist()
description: OPFS is evictable under storage pressure (VISION constraint 5). Request persistence at boot (navigator.storage.persist()), surface granted/denied + usage/quota in quipu_wasm_status, and nudge toward quipu_export_db / git push when denied.
acceptance_criteria: Status reports persistence state and quota; request made once, not nagged.
close_reason: navigator.storage.persist() requested once at bind; persisted/usage/quota surfaced in quipu_wasm_status with export nudge when evictable.

title: Background-tab throttling: measure and mitigate for agent tabs
description: VISION constraint 4: unfocused tabs get CPU-throttled; await-fetch LLM loops mostly survive but Pyodide/tool work may crawl. Measure a background agent tab's wall-clock vs focused, document findings, and if needed move tool execution into Workers (unthrottled) or recommend tiled windows / separate profile in the README.
acceptance_criteria: Measured numbers in docs; mitigation implemented or explicitly ruled unnecessary.

title: The weft: burst synthesis view and one-click write-back
description: VISION v3: at burst end, a synthesis pass runs across the parallel threads — dashboard view comparing fleet_report results (and diffs once per-agent branches exist), a synthesize action that hands all results to the operator's agent for a combined answer, and one-click write-back of what the burst learned into the quipu graph (episodes tagged with burst id).
acceptance_criteria: After a 3-agent burst: one dashboard view shows all results side by side, 'synthesize' produces a combined summary in the operator conversation, 'write back' lands tagged episodes in the store.
close_reason: fleet_synthesize collects finished results; dashboard Synthesize injects them into the operator conversation; fleet_writeback records takeaways as Burst-tagged quipu episodes. Verified: synthesis payload, writeback queryable in graph, dashboard control renders.
